//: List of the conditions compared by the bench: one entry per browser tool, plus a control without a browser.
Adding a tool = adding an entry. Fields:
id             short identifier, used in folder names (runs/<id>-<n>/).
name           display name used in reports.
homepage       official README the install steps were copied from (2026-11-04).
skill          which skill variant the agent gets: 'full' (with the browser steps) or 'control' (without them).
prerequisites  commands to run ONCE, by hand, on the machine (global installs, browser extensions). The launcher only prints them.
setup          commands the launcher runs inside each fresh trial workspace, before the agent starts (e.g. project-level skill install).
mcpServers     MCP servers given to Claude Code for this condition only (--mcp-config + --strict-mcp-config).
claudeArgs     extra command-line flags for `claude` (e.g. --chrome).
needsRealChrome true when the tool drives the user's own Chrome through an extension: it may not run unattended.
platforms      optional list of supported OSes (Node's process.platform). The launcher skips the condition elsewhere.
extraContext   OPTIONAL extra instructions or configuration for this tool. Empty in the first, 'raw' test:
every tool is installed exactly as its README says, with the same skill for all.
Setup note: install commands were made project-level where the tool allows it, so that one tool's skill
never leaks into another condition. The launcher warns if browser skills are found in ~/.claude/skills.
signature      how the bench recognises this tool in the session log: `bash` = command names the agent runs
through the Bash tool, `tools` = prefixes of tool names. An attempt FAILS if the tool was called
and not a single call succeeded (not installed, extension not connected...). An agent that never
calls its tool is not a failure: that is its behaviour, and the trial counts.
healthCheck    commands run by the launcher, in a temporary folder, once the dev server is up and BEFORE the agent
starts. If one fails, the attempt fails without spending any token. Commands copied from each README
(2026-11-06). Empty when the tool cannot be checked by a script (MCP servers are checked in the
session's init event; Claude in Chrome goes through a browser extension).
Playwriter: `playwriter session new` opens a session through the extension, so it fails if the
extension is not connected, and a session is ready when the agent starts (decided 2026-11-16).
forbidden      OPTIONAL list of {pattern, reason}: a Bash command matching `pattern` (a regular expression) means the agent
left the condition (e.g. Playwriter without its extension). The launcher stops the session at once and the
attempt FAILS (decided 2026-11-16, after the first Playwriter trial ran headless).
variantOf      OPTIONAL id of the condition this one is a variant of (same tool, different environment). Its id must
not start with the other id followed by '-', or the failed attempts of the two would be counted together.
strict-control (17/11): the control as D82 meant it. The first controls (Opus and Sonnet) built their own loop
with the Chrome or Edge installed on the machine, driven headless from a script; that condition stays, as
'control' (the homemade loop). This one forbids any browser, in commands and in the files the agent writes.

tools.name: Strict control (no browser at all)
tools.extraContext: This condition has no browser. Do not launch, install or drive any browser, in any mode: no Chrome, Edge or Chromium, with or without a window (headless), and no browser library (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, WebDriver), even one already installed on the machine. Build the page from ./mockup/design.json and the captures, by reading the code you write. The bench stops the session at the first command or file that uses a browser, and the trial is lost.
